        "statement": "Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions (x^0 = c t). Let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) and let W := {x^1 > |x^0|} be the right wedge. Let Phi and n be the Rindler chart and congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b): Phi(theta,rho,y,z) = (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2 with inverse rho = sqrt((x^1)^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x^1+x^0)/(x^1-x^0)), pullback metric -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, and acceleration field a_cg = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho. Fix rho_0 > 0 and real y_0,z_0, and let O be the congruence worldline rho = rho_0, y = y_0, z = z_0, parametrized by its proper time tau with theta = c tau/rho_0; by def-sr-proper-acceleration its proper acceleration is c^2/rho_0. Write U(q) := q^0 + q^1 and V(q) := q^0 - q^1 for events q, so that U = rho e^{theta} and V = -rho e^{-theta} on W, and write <= and J^+, J^- for the causal reachability relations of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space. Then, conditionally on the adopted model: (i) Chart domain and light rays. Phi is a smooth bijection of R x (0,inf) x R^2 onto W with the stated smooth inverse, so the chart domain is exactly W and rho = 0 is not part of its coordinate domain. The boundary of W in the affine model is {x^1 = |x^0|}, with arbitrary x^2,x^3: it is the union of the two null half-planes {x^1 = x^0 >= 0} and {x^1 = -x^0 >= 0}. These half-planes are portions of the full null planes appearing as causal horizons in (ii); the full planes are not the wedge boundary. Along the worldline rho = rho_0 one has V = -rho_0 e^{-theta} -> 0^- and U -> +infinity as theta -> +infinity, while U = rho_0 e^{theta} -> 0^+ and V -> -infinity as theta -> -infinity. The future null straight lines of the model that lie in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0 and meet O are exactly the lines of constant V (on which dtheta = +drho/rho) and the lines of constant U (on which dtheta = -drho/rho). (ii) Causal horizons. An event q satisfies q <= p for some event p of O if and only if V(q) < 0; an event q satisfies p <= q for some event p of O if and only if U(q) > 0. Consequently no event with V(q) >= 0 can ever influence O; this set contains the null plane {x^1 = x^0}, the left wedge {x^1 < -|x^0|} and the future wedge {x^0 > |x^1|}; and no event with U(q) <= 0 can ever be influenced by O, a set containing the null plane {x^1 = -x^0}, the left wedge and the past wedge {x^0 < -|x^1|}. The null plane {x^1 = x^0} is the boundary of the causal past of O (the future horizon: the surface its worldline approaches as theta -> +infinity), and the null plane {x^1 = -x^0} is the boundary of the causal future of O (the past horizon); every event of the left wedge is causally unrelated to O in both directions. The same criteria with O any other congruence worldline rho = rho_1, y = y_1, z = z_1 hold verbatim: the constants rho_0, y_0, z_0 do not enter. (iii) Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector. Fix rho_m > 0 with rho_m != rho_0 and let R_m be the congruence worldline rho = rho_m, y = y_0, z = z_0 (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with O, with proper acceleration c^2/rho_m). Let e_- be the event of O at parameter theta_e (so tau(e_-) = rho_0 theta_e/c up to the base point of tau), let q_m be the event of R_m lying on the future null straight line from e_- in the plane y = y_0, z = z_0, and let e_+ be the event of O lying on the future null straight line from q_m; the reflection at q_m is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving R_m's motion unchanged, as in def-sr-operational-radar-protocol. Then e_-, q_m, e_+ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of q_m is theta_m = theta_e + |log(rho_m/rho_0)|, the return event satisfies theta(e_+) = theta_e + 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| and (theta_e + theta(e_+))/2 = theta_m, so the round trip lasts 2|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in Rindler time and (2rho_0/c)|log(rho_m/rho_0)| in O's proper time. The radar protocol therefore assigns to q_m the radar time tau_rad(q_m) = (rho_0/c) theta_m plus the base constant of tau and the radar distance rho_rad(q_m) = rho_0 |log(rho_m/rho_0)|; within this coaxial family the radar-time level sets are exactly the Rindler simultaneity slices theta = const, i.e. the rest slices of the congruence (def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance). The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice theta = theta_m the two worldlines are at rest distance |rho_m - rho_0|, whereas for rho_m = 2rho_0 the radar distance is rho_0 log 2 < rho_0, because log is strictly increasing and e > 2 implies log 2 < log e = 1 (cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three, thm-natural-logarithm-laws); For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r=\\rho_m/\\rho_0$, one has $\\log r<r-1$ when $r>1$ and $-\\log r>1-r$ when $0<r<1$.         "statement": "## Setup\n\nThe experiment used $^7\\mathrm{Li}^+$ ions from a Penning ion gauge source, accelerated to $58.6\\,\\mathrm{MeV/u}$ and stored in the ESR at nominal $\\beta=0.338$. About $10^7$ to $10^8$ ions were stored, with an estimated metastable fraction below $1\\%$. The metastable $3S_1$ lifetime was $15$–$30\\,\\mathrm{s}$ in the ring, compared with $50\\,\\mathrm{s}$ in vacuum. The Lambda system used the transitions $3S_1(F=3/2)\\to3P_2(F=5/2)$ and $3S_1(F=5/2)\\to3P_2(F=5/2)$. Parallel and antiparallel beams near $386\\,\\mathrm{nm}$ and $780\\,\\mathrm{nm}$ addressed its two legs; an additional $780\\,\\mathrm{nm}$ beam repumped ions into the system.\n\n## Procedure\n\nThe parallel beam was generated by doubling a $772\\,\\mathrm{nm}$ Ti:Sa laser locked to an iodine marker previously calibrated with a frequency comb against a rubidium clock. The antiparallel diode laser was offset-locked to a rubidium reference, with a $600\\,\\mathrm{MHz}$ tuning range. Polarization-maintaining fibers transported the beams. Motorized stages controlled angles and positions to $20\\,\\mu\\mathrm{rad}$ and $50\\,\\mu\\mathrm{m}$; scrapers established laser/ion overlap within $80\\,\\mu\\mathrm{rad}$. Photomultipliers counted fluorescence in four successive $100\\,\\mu\\mathrm{s}$ configurations: both excitation beams, antiparallel only, parallel only, and neither. Dark counts were subtracted, then the separate-beam background was subtracted from the both-beam spectrum. Optical-optical double resonance selected ions for which both Lambda legs were resonant at the same velocity. To compensate metastable depletion, an $81$-point scan was paused after $69$ points for injection and cooling. Figure 2 shows an example averaged over $44$ scans, with $49\\,\\mathrm{MHz}$ laboratory linewidth and $35\\,\\mathrm{MHz}$ rest-frame linewidth. The authors fitted $40$ spectra with Lorentzians on linear backgrounds and formed a weighted average. Raw count tables, fit weights, a covariance matrix and a complete likelihood are not published in this report.\n\n## Observations\n\nTable I gives the frequency estimates, in MHz, $\\nu_1=546455143.0$, $\\nu_2=546474960.7$, $\\nu_a=384225534.98$ and $\\nu_p=777210326.98$. The rest-frame inputs $\\nu_1,\\nu_2$ come from earlier measurements cited as references 21–22; those papers were not retrieved or read here. The authors reported no significant residual asymmetry; simulated background linearization was assigned $0.5\\,\\mathrm{MHz}$. The excess linewidth, about five times the expected width, was attributed mainly to drift-induced fluorescence. The $0.6\\,\\mathrm{MHz}$ statistical entry comes from the weighted analysis of forty fitted spectra, not forty independent raw clock readings.   (batch 16) rather than from the published Kirchhoff formula, because the exact

  consumes; the published Kirchhoff/Duhamel items were read and their statements
  matched to the same mathematics (see the coverage harvest rows).
- **Normalisation checked twice.** With `W = c^{-2} ∂_t² − Δ` one has
  `□_c = c² W`; the source term of W2 is `c² ∫_{t_0}^t H_{h(·,v)}(x, t−v) dv`,
  which is exactly the two-source Duhamel integral
  `∫_0^t (t−s) M_{c(t−s)} f(·,s)(x) ds` with `f = c² h` applied to
  `□_c u = f`. Teschl Corollary 7.3 and Ivrii (9.1.11)–(9.1.12) both compute
  this with the Leibniz rule, with **no spatial compact-support hypothesis** —
  the published `thm-wave-duhamel-principle` is the compactly supported
  special case, which is why the general smooth source is proved here.

The large arc contributes at most $\\pi R\\sup_{|z|=R,\\operatorname{Im}z\\ge0}|\\chi_{jk}|/(R-|\\omega|)\\to0$ by the $|z|^{-2}$ bound.         "statement": "Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A.         "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$), the convention of the Lebesgue interface used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\\ge3$, let $\\Phi$ be the fundamental solution of $-\\Delta$ on $\\mathbb R^n$ normalised by $-\\Delta T_\\Phi=\\delta_0$ ([[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]]), so that for $z\\ne0$\n$$\\Phi(z)=\\frac{|z|^{2-n}}{(n-2)\\omega_{n-1}},\\qquad \\nabla\\Phi(z)=-\\frac{z}{\\omega_{n-1}|z|^n},\\qquad |\\nabla\\Phi(z)|=\\frac{1}{\\omega_{n-1}|z|^{n-1}},$$\nlet $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb R^n)$ be real, measurable and zero $\\lambda_n$-almost everywhere outside a closed ball $\\overline B_R(0)=\\{x:|x|\\le R\\}$ of finite radius $R>0$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), and let\n$$Nf(x)=\\int_{\\mathbb R^n}\\Phi(x-y)f(y)\\,d\\lambda_n(y)$$\nbe the Newtonian potential ([[def-newtonian-potential]]). Then:\n(a) [Representation and differentiability off the far field] for every $x\\in\\mathbb R^n$ with $|x|>2R$ the integral $\\int_{\\mathbb R^n}\\nabla\\Phi(x-y)f(y)\\,d\\lambda_n(y)$ is absolutely convergent, the function $Nf$ is differentiable at $x$ with\n$$\\nabla(Nf)(x)=\\int_{\\mathbb R^n}\\nabla\\Phi(x-y)f(y)\\,d\\lambda_n(y),$$\nand $x\\mapsto\\nabla(Nf)(x)$ is continuous on the open set $\\{x:|x|>2R\\}$;\n(b) [Decay bound] for every $x$ with $|x|>2R$,\n$$|\\nabla(Nf)(x)|\\le\\frac{2^{n-1}\\|f\\|_1}{\\omega_{n-1}|x|^{n-1}},\\qquad \\|f\\|_1:=\\int_{\\mathbb R^n}|f|\\,d\\lambda_n;$$\n(c) [Scope] the hypothesis is compact support together with $L^1$-integrability; no boundedness of $f$ is assumed, and nothing is asserted at points with $|x|\\le2R$ (where the kernel singularity may meet the support of $f$).",
        "strategy": "Fix $x_0$ with $|x_0|>2R$ and choose $0<\\delta<|x_0|-2R$. On the full open ball $U=B_\\delta(x_0)$, every $y\\in\\overline B_R$ obeys $|x-y|\\ge |x_0|-\\delta-R=:c>0$. Thus both $|\\Phi(x-y)f(y)|\\le c^{2-n}|f(y)|/((n-2)\\omega_{n-1})$ and $|\\partial_i\\Phi(x-y)f(y)|\\le c^{1-n}|f(y)|/\\omega_{n-1}$ hold throughout $U$, outside the single null set on which $f$ may fail to vanish off $\\overline B_R$. Equivalently reset $f$ to zero on that set without changing any integral. The majorants are integrable; the kernel and its coordinate derivatives are continuous off zero and their products with measurable $f$ are measurable ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Restricting to each sufficiently short coordinate interval through any $x\\in U$, [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign]] yields $\\partial_iNf(x)=\\int\\partial_i\\Phi(x-y)f(y)dy$. For any sequence $x_m\\to x$ in $U$, the derivative integrands converge almost everywhere and have the same full-neighbourhood majorant $c^{1-n}|f|/\\omega_{n-1}$. [[thm-dominated-convergence]] therefore proves continuity of each partial derivative as a function of all coordinates on $U$, not merely along coordinate lines. [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]] now gives total differentiability and the displayed gradient representation; the continuous vector of partials is the gradient ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). As $x_0$ was arbitrary, (a) holds throughout the stated far field. For (b), $|x-y|\\ge |x|-R>|x|/2$ on the support, so $|\\nabla\\Phi(x-y)|\\le2^{n-1}/(\\omega_{n-1}|x|^{n-1})$; integrating against $|f|$ gives the stated bound.         "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$) for the Lebesgue and product-measure interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\\ge2$, let $p\\in\\mathbb R^n$, and let $u\\in L^1_{\\mathrm{loc}}(\\mathbb R^n)$ be continuous on $\\mathbb R^n\\setminus\\{p\\}$ and of class $C^1$ there, with each classical partial derivative $\\partial_iu:\\mathbb R^n\\setminus\\{p\\}\\to\\mathbb R$ (extended by $0$ at $p$) again in $L^1_{\\mathrm{loc}}(\\mathbb R^n)$. Then for every $i=1,\\dots,n$, with $T_u\\in\\mathcal D'(\\mathbb R^n)$ the regular distribution of $u$ ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $\\partial_i$ the distributional derivative ([[def-distributional-derivative]]),\n$$\\partial_iT_u=T_{\\partial_iu}\\qquad\\text{in }\\mathcal D'(\\mathbb R^n),$$\nthat is, $\\langle\\partial_iT_u,\\psi\\rangle=\\int_{\\mathbb R^n}\\partial_iu\\,\\psi\\,d\\lambda_n$ for every $\\psi\\in C_c^\\infty(\\mathbb R^n)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). The value assigned to $\\partial_iu$ at the single point $p$ is immaterial, because a singleton is Lebesgue null ([[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]], [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]], [[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]). Both hypotheses are used: $u$ must be locally integrable and continuous away from $p$, and each classical partial must be locally integrable; the lemma is asserted for one exceptional point, not for an exceptional set of positive surface measure.",
        "strategy": "The given $u$ is continuous off $p$, hence Borel there; assigning a finite value at $p$ makes a Borel representative on all of $\\mathbb R^n$. Each classical partial is continuous off $p$ and is extended by zero there, hence is also Borel. Thus the products with tests below are Borel, so the cited Borel product-measure identification applies directly. Fix $i$ and $\\psi\\in C_c^\\infty(\\mathbb R^n)$; both $\\partial_iu\\,\\psi$ and $u\\,\\partial_i\\psi$ are integrable on $\\mathbb R^n$: for the first, $|\\partial_iu\\,\\psi|\\le\\|\\psi\\|_\\infty|\\partial_iu|$ with $\\partial_iu\\in L^1_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ and $\\psi$ compactly supported, and for the second $|u\\,\\partial_i\\psi|\\le\\|\\partial_i\\psi\\|_\\infty|u|$ with $u\\in L^1_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Split $\\mathbb R^n=\\mathbb R\\times\\mathbb R^{n-1}$ into the $i$-th coordinate $t$ and the remaining coordinates $y$; identify the Lebesgue measure with the product measure ([[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]], [[def-product-measure-on-sigma-finite-spaces]]), so that [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] applies to both integrable functions. Let $Y$ be the set of $y$ for which the line $\\{(t,y):t\\in\\mathbb R\\}$ meets $p$: it is the single transverse point $y=p'$, a $\\lambda_{n-1}$-null set by [[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]] (this is where $n\\ge2$ is used: for $n=1$ there are no transverse coordinates and the case would have to be argued separately by absolute continuity). For every $y\\notin Y$ the line misses $p$, so $t\\mapsto u(t,y)$ is $C^1$ on $\\mathbb R$ with derivative $t\\mapsto\\partial_iu(t,y)$, and $t\\mapsto u(t,y)\\psi(t,y)$ is $C^1$ with compact support; [[thm-integration-by-parts]] (equivalently the fundamental theorem, [[thm-ftc-first-part]]) on an interval containing the support gives\n$$\\int_{\\mathbb R}\\partial_iu(t,y)\\psi(t,y)\\,dt=-\\int_{\\mathbb R}u(t,y)\\partial_i\\psi(t,y)\\,dt.$$\nThis holds for every $y\\notin Y$, hence almost everywhere. Fubini's theorem applied to the two integrable functions gives\n$$\\int_{\\mathbb R^n}\\partial_iu\\,\\psi\\,d\\lambda_n=\\int_{\\mathbb R^{n-1}}\\!\\!\\int_{\\mathbb R}(\\partial_iu\\,\\psi)\\,dt\\,dy=-\\int_{\\mathbb R^{n-1}}\\!\\!\\int_{\\mathbb R}(u\\,\\partial_i\\psi)\\,dt\\,dy=-\\int_{\\mathbb R^n}u\\,\\partial_i\\psi\\,d\\lambda_n.$$\nThe right-hand side is $-\\langle T_u,\\partial_i\\psi\\rangle=\\langle\\partial_iT_u,\\psi\\rangle$ by the definition of the distributional derivative ([[def-distribution]]), and the left-hand side is $\\langle T_{\\partial_iu},\\psi\\rangle$ ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]). Hence $\\partial_iT_u=T_{\\partial_iu}$. Measurability of $\\partial_iu$ is not assumed beyond the stated $L^1_{\\mathrm{loc}}$ membership of its extension: on $\\mathbb R^n\\setminus\\{p\\}$ it is the pointwise limit of the difference quotients of the measurable $u$, hence measurable there by the closure properties of measurable functions ([[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and the single point $p$ does not affect the classes ([[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]). Then:\n(a) [Finiteness] the three quantities\n$$\\frac{\\varepsilon_0}{2}\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\\,d\\lambda_3,\\qquad \\frac12\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\rho\\varphi\\,d\\lambda_3,\\qquad +\\frac{1}{2\\varepsilon_0}\\iint_{\\mathbb R^3\\times\\mathbb R^3}\\Phi(x-y)\\rho(x)\\rho(y)\\,d(\\lambda_3\\times\\lambda_3)(x,y)$$\nare finite real numbers;\n(b) [Identity] they are equal:\n$$\\frac{\\varepsilon_0}{2}\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\\,d\\lambda_3=\\frac12\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\rho\\varphi\\,d\\lambda_3=\\frac{1}{2\\varepsilon_0}\\iint_{\\mathbb R^3\\times\\mathbb R^3}\\Phi(x-y)\\rho(x)\\rho(y)\\,d(\\lambda_3\\times\\lambda_3)(x,y).$$\nThe last expression is the **external assembly work** of the ideal quasistatic bookkeeping family $\\rho_s=s\\rho$, $\\varphi_s=s\\varphi$ for $0\\le s\\le1$. An added test charge brought from infinity, where the potential is zero, has electric-force work $-dq\\,\\varphi_s$ by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-work]]; the balancing external work is $+dq\\,\\varphi_s$. Therefore $W_{\\rm ext}=\\int_0^1s\\,ds\\int\\rho\\varphi=\\tfrac12\\int\\rho\\varphi$. Both signs of $\\rho$ are allowed. The symmetric double kernel gives the equivalent ordered-pair interpretation of the factor $1/2$.\n(c) [Scope] the identity is a statement about the ideal quasi-static assembly of a compactly supported $C^1$ charge distribution in vacuum, all sources being held in place by external support ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]). It asserts no time-dependent work, no radiation, no material or stability model, and it does not identify the field energy with the rest mass of any particle; the point-source limit is treated separately and is divergent (see the point-charge field energy of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d)).",

Let $E:\\mathbb R\\to\\mathbb R^3$ be the electric-field history in the material rest frame, read componentwise in its spatial basis ([[def-em-fields]]), and let $P$ be the polarisation response declared by the model.\n(a) [Causal response] If the kernel of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) satisfies $K\\in L^1(0,\\infty;\\mathbb R^{3\\times3})$, then for every bounded continuous history $E$ the response $P(t)=\\varepsilon_0\\int_0^\\infty K(s)E(t-s)\\,ds$ is well defined for every $t$, bounded and continuous, linear in $E$, and causal: histories equal on $(-\\infty,t_0]$ produce responses equal on $(-\\infty,t_0]$.\n(b) [Transfer function and dispersion relations] If $K$ is smooth with compact support in $(0,\\infty)$, the transfer function $\\chi(z)=\\int_0^\\infty K(s)e^{izs}\\,ds$ is entire, satisfies $\\chi(-\\omega)=\\overline{\\chi(\\omega)}$ for real $\\omega$, obeys $|\\chi_{jk}(z)|\\le\\|K_{jk}''\\|_{L^1}|z|^{-2}$ for $z\\ne0$ with $\\operatorname{Im}z\\ge0$ (with the whole-plane bound carrying the exponential factor $e^{b\\max(0,-\\operatorname{Im}z)}$ when $\\operatorname{supp}K\\subseteq(0,b)$), and its entries satisfy the principal-value dispersion relations of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]](b). If $K$ is locally absolutely continuous on $[0,\\infty)$ with $K,K'\\in L^1$ and $sK\\in L^1$, then $\\chi$ is holomorphic on the open upper half-plane, continuous with continuous first derivative on the real boundary, obeys the stated growth bound, and satisfies the same pair of relations; an instantaneous real part $\\chi_\\infty$ may be added to the model, and the relations apply to $\\chi_{\\mathrm{total}}-\\chi_\\infty$ for $\\chi_{\\mathrm{total}}=\\chi_\\infty+\\chi$.\n(c) [Finitely-subtracted and polynomial branches] For each specified integer $n\\ge1$ for which the full hypotheses of [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]] hold for the declared response transfer function, its $n$-subtracted relations apply entrywise.         "statement": "(a) [Dimensional exclusion of $E=\\varepsilon_0D$] In the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: the electric constant $\\varepsilon_0=(\\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ carries $\\mathrm F\\,\\mathrm m^{-1}=\\mathrm C^2\\mathrm s^2\\,\\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\\mathrm m^{-3}$, the displacement $D$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]] carries $\\mathrm C\\,\\mathrm m^{-2}$, and the electric field $E$ of [[def-em-fields]] carries $\\mathrm V\\,\\mathrm m^{-1}=\\mathrm{kg}\\,\\mathrm m\\,\\mathrm s^{-2}\\mathrm C^{-1}$. The product $\\varepsilon_0D$ therefore carries $\\mathrm F\\,\\mathrm C\\,\\mathrm m^{-3}=\\mathrm C^3\\mathrm s^2\\,\\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\\mathrm m^{-5}$, which is not the dimension of $E$: the proposed identification $E=\\varepsilon_0D$ fails dimensionally in SI and cannot be a field relation of the framework.\n(b) [Units do not determine the law] Solving the definition $D=\\varepsilon_0E+P$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]] gives $E=(D-P)/\\varepsilon_0$, which in vacuum ($P=0$) reads $E=\\varepsilon_0^{-1}D$. Any proposed law $E=\\eta D$ with a constant $\\eta>0$ of dimension $\\mathrm V\\,\\mathrm m\\,\\mathrm C^{-1}$ is dimensionally admissible; dimensional consistency therefore does not identify $\\eta$, and it does not determine whether the response is local, linear or instantaneous. In the model of [[post-em-material-closure]] the scalar relation is $D=\\varepsilon E$, i.e. $\\eta=\\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $\\varepsilon$ (or $\\chi_e=\\varepsilon/\\varepsilon_0-1$) is fixed by the declared material model, not by units.\n(c) [Frequency-domain symbols are not instantaneous coefficients] In the memory branch of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) the response is a causal convolution in time; a scalar $\\varepsilon(\\omega)$ introduced in the harmonic description acts on the Fourier components of the field history in the material rest frame. The framework therefore does not read $\\varepsilon(\\omega)$ as an instantaneous multiplicative coefficient in the time domain: doing so silently replaces the convolution by an instantaneous law and is a model-identification error of the same kind as (a).\n(d) [Scope] A dimensional and model-identification statement about the framework's own conventions; it asserts no measurement, no material property and no empirical claim.",
        "strategy": "**Proof technique:** direct dimensional computation and immediate consequences of the definitions. (a): the units of $\\varepsilon_0$, $D$ and $E$ are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the derived-unit identities $\\mathrm F=\\mathrm C\\,\\mathrm V^{-1}$ and $\\mathrm V=\\mathrm{kg}\\,\\mathrm m^2\\mathrm s^{-2}\\mathrm C^{-1}$ give $\\mathrm F\\,\\mathrm m^{-1}=\\mathrm C^2\\mathrm s^2\\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $\\mathrm V\\,\\mathrm m^{-1}=\\mathrm{kg}\\,\\mathrm m\\,\\mathrm s^{-2}\\mathrm C^{-1}$; multiplying the first by $\\mathrm C\\,\\mathrm m^{-2}$ gives $\\mathrm F\\,\\mathrm C\\,\\mathrm m^{-3}$, a different combination of the base units $\\mathrm{kg},\\mathrm m,\\mathrm s,\\mathrm C$. (b): $D=\\varepsilon_0E+P$ is a definition of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]], and solving it is elementary algebra; the vacuum constant $\\eta=\\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ has the dimension of $E/D$ while being a model constant. (c): the memory branch is a convolution in time by [[post-em-material-closure]](c); a harmonic symbol acts on Fourier components and does not define an instantaneous coefficient.         "statement": "Let the laboratory frame, coordinates $(x,y,z)$ and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $S=\\{z=0\\}\\cap\\Omega$ be a stationary planar interface with unit normal $n=e_z$ pointing from the side $\\Omega_-=\\{z<0\\}$ to the side $\\Omega_+=\\{z>0\\}$. ## Inventory decisions (recorded, not silent)

- `def-em-moving-circuit-geometry` (definition): the C2 moving material circuit (compact finite
  elementary Green region, embedded swept patch, nonzero normal, single-valued C1 material
  velocity), its flux and its emf line integral with units, the no-singularity-crossing

- `lem-em-newtonian-linkage-symmetry` (mathematics): absolute convergence, equality of the three
  integral representations and symmetry/bilinearity of the Newtonian linkage pairing for smooth
  compact vector fields, by Tonelli/Fubini plus local integrability of the kernel.
- `lem-em-newtonian-curl-field-energy` (mathematics): `div A = 0`, `-Delta A = mu0 J`,
  the decay `|curl A| <= C(1+|x|^2)^{-1}` and the exact energy identity
  `int |curl A|^2 = mu0 int <A,J> >= 0` for `A = mu0 N(J)`, `div J = 0`, by one ball excision
  with a vanishing boundary flux.
- `pthm-em-motional-emf` (physics theorem): the transport formula of the moving-patch lemma
  plus the frozen-patch Faraday clause of the integral-Maxwell theorem give
  `emf(t) = -Phi_B'(t)` at every time in a compact no-crossing subinterval; the work-per-charge
  reading uses the adopted Lorentz coupling.
- `post-em-circuit-approximation` (postulate): fixed finite branch data, constant symmetric L,
  positive-definite C and positive-semidefinite R, the Faraday/capacitive/Ohmic branch
  relations, Kirchhoff laws, the declared quasistatic smallness condition with the explicit
  warning that no error theorem follows from it, SI units and the full exclusion list
  (radiation, leakage, distributed, nonlinear, hysteretic, proximity effects). No fabricated
  proof; `provenance.proof: not-applicable`.
- `pthm-em-inductance-reciprocity` (physics theorem): finite reciprocal linkage coefficients of
  fixed compact smooth conserved current profiles, the linear linkage identity, and
  `U(I) = (1/2) I^T L I = (1/2 mu0) int |B_J|^2 >= 0` with vanishing exactly for vanishing
  current and positive definiteness exactly for pointwise-independent profiles; the thin-wire
  and singular self-inductance exclusions are explicit.
- `pthm-em-inductor-energy` (physics theorem): the exact terminal-energy bookkeeping
  `int V.I dt = Delta(1/2 I^T L I)` for C1 currents and constant symmetric L in fixed geometry,
  and the identification of the quadratic form with the frozen magnetic field energy of the
  smooth-profile realization; changing geometry needs the mechanical work term and is excluded.
- `pthm-em-rl-lc-dynamics` (physics theorem): the unique C1 solution of the scalar RL equation
  with continuous source voltage and its power split; the explicit C2 LC oscillator, its exact
  initial values, the cosine-sine form, and conservation of `1/2 L I^2 + Q^2/(2C)` with the
  capacitive energy identified through the two-conductor reading of the capacitance theorem.
  Scope: lumped model only, no general networks, no radiation or distributed effects.
- `texp-em-sliding-bar-emf` (thought experiment): the ideal rigid rectangular circuit with a
  frictionless bar at prescribed speed in a uniform static field; `emf = -B0 l x'(t)`,
  `F = I l B0 e1` from the adopted continuum force density, and the exact instantaneous
  power balance `F.v + emf I = 0`; no measurement, no bar dynamics.
- `ex-em-transformer-idealization` (example): the two-circuit quadratic energy and power
  identity, the realization bound `|M| <= sqrt(L1 L2)` (with the perfect-linkage null direction
  carrying zero current), and the explicitly adopted common-flux ideal-transformer relations
  `V1/N1 = V2/N2 = Phi_c-dot` with the corresponding induced-emf signs; leakage, resistance,
  core loss, stray capacitance and magnetising current are excluded.
- `ex-em-rl-time-response` (example): the constant-voltage RL transient
  `I = V0/R + (I0 - V0/R) exp(-R(t-t0)/L)`, verified by differentiation with uniqueness
  inherited from the RL theorem, with the limit statement correctly qualified by the interval
  hypothesis.

        "statement": "Let the laboratory region $\\Omega\\times I$ and its inertial chart, the field objects $E,B$ and the units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], with $c>0$.\n\n(a) [Moving material circuit] A moving material circuit on the laboratory region is the data $(D,r,v)$ specified as follows. $D\\subseteq\\mathbb R^2$ is a compact finite elementary Green region with its positive boundary orientation; $r:D\\times I\\to\\Omega$ extends to a $C^2$ map on a neighbourhood of $D\\times I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $r_u\\times r_v\\ne0$ on the interior of $D$ and $r(\\cdot,t)$ injective on the interior of $D$ for every $t$ (embedded material sheet); and $v$ is a $C^1$ vector field on a neighbourhood of the swept set $\\{(r(u,w,t),t):(u,w)\\in D,\\ t\\in I\\}$ in $\\Omega\\times I$ satisfying the single-valued condition $v(r(u,w,t),t)=\\partial_tr(u,w,t)$ for all $(u,w)\\in D$ and all $t\\in I$. In the notation of [[def-em-moving-patch]] the map $r$ is the swept moving patch and $v$ is its single-valued velocity; material points of the circuit are the images of the parameter points $(u,w)$.\n\n(b) [Surface, boundary and flux] For $t\\in I$ put $S(t):=r(D,t)$ and let $C(t):=\\partial S(t)$ carry the boundary orientation induced by the positive orientation of $D$. For $B$ of class $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the swept set, the magnetic flux of the circuit at time $t$ is the parametrized flux\n$$\\Phi_B(t):=\\int_D\\bigl\\langle B(r(u,w,t),t),\\,r_u(u,w,t)\\times r_v(u,w,t)\\bigr\\rangle\\,du\\,dw$$\nof [[def-em-moving-patch]]; its unit is the weber, $\\mathrm{Wb}=\\mathrm T\\,\\mathrm m^2$.\n\n(c) [Electromotive force] For $E,B$ continuous on a neighbourhood of the swept set, the electromotive force (emf) of the circuit at time $t$ is the vector line integral over the oriented closed path $C(t)$\n$$\\mathrm{emf}(t):=\\oint_{C(t)}\\bigl\\langle E(\\cdot,t)+v(\\cdot,t)\\times B(\\cdot,t),\\,d\\mathbf r\\bigr\\rangle$$\nin the convention of [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]], with the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; its unit is the volt, $1\\,\\mathrm V=1\\,\\mathrm{kg}\\,\\mathrm m^2\\,\\mathrm s^{-3}\\mathrm A^{-1}$. Under the framework's Lorentz coupling the integrand is the force per unit charge on a charge moving with the conductor material; the definition itself only names the line integral.\n\n(d) [Scope and exclusions] The fields are assumed of the stated regularity on a neighbourhood of the swept set: circuits passing through a point charge, a curve or surface singularity, or any place where the fields fail to be of that regularity are excluded (no singularity crossings). When the emf is interpreted through the framework's relativistic Lorentz coupling, material speeds are required to be subluminal, $|v|<c$. The definition asserts no conservation law and no relation between $\\mathrm{emf}$ and $\\Phi_B'$; in particular the flux concerns the single field $B$ and the emf the pair $(E,B)$, and neither object is claimed independent of the chosen parametrization.",
        "strategy": "Explicit type/domain/convention definition. The integrand of $\\Phi_B$ is continuous on the compact parameter region $D$ because $B$ and $r$ are continuous on a neighbourhood of $D\\times I$ and $r_u,r_v$ are continuous; the flux is therefore a Riemann integral over a compact Jordan-measurable region in the moving-patch convention of [[def-em-moving-patch]]. The line integral is taken in the piecewise $C^1$ path convention of [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]; the $C^2$ extension of $r$ and the single-valued $C^1$ condition on $v$ are exactly the hypotheses under which the moving-patch definition and its transport lemma are stated. Clause (d) records the no-singularity-crossing hypothesis and the subluminal condition; neither is used in the definition of the flux itself.         "statement": "Assume Countable Choice ($\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$) as carried by the Tonelli, Fubini and polar/kernel-local-integrability interfaces cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $N$ be the Newtonian potential transform of [[def-newtonian-potential]], so that for real $f\\in C_c^\\infty(\\mathbb R^3;\\mathbb R)$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]])\n$$Nf(x)=\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\frac{f(y)}{4\\pi|x-y|}\\,d\\lambda_3(y),$$\nand let $\\langle\\cdot,\\cdot\\rangle$ be the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. For $u,v\\in C_c^\\infty(\\mathbb R^3;\\mathbb R^3)$ write $Nu:=(Nu_1,Nu_2,Nu_3)$ componentwise, so that the linkage pairing is the map\n$$B(u,v):=\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\langle u(x),Nv(x)\\rangle\\,d\\lambda_3(x).$$\nThen all three integrals\n$$\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\langle u(x),Nv(x)\\rangle\\,d\\lambda_3(x),\\qquad\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\langle Nu(x),v(x)\\rangle\\,d\\lambda_3(x),\\qquad\\frac1{4\\pi}\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\frac{\\langle u(x),v(y)\\rangle}{|x-y|}\\,d\\lambda_3(y)\\,d\\lambda_3(x)$$\nconverge absolutely ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]]) and have the same value; therefore $B$ is well defined, real-valued, symmetric, $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$, and bilinear over $\\mathbb R$ in each argument. In particular the common value of the three integrals is unchanged by exchanging the two density fields $u$ and $v$ and the two integration variables.",
        "strategy": "Absolute convergence first, then Fubini. Choose $R>0$ such that both supports are contained in the open ball $B_R(0)$. Assign $g(0)=0$ and $g(z)=|z|^{-1}$ otherwise. This is Borel, and the kernel-local-integrability supplier [[lem-laplace-fundamental-kernel-is-locally-integrable]] gives $K_R:=\\int_{B_{2R}}g(z)d\\lambda_3(z)<\\infty$. For each $x\\in B_R$, the translation $z=x-y$ carries $B_R$ into $B_{2R}$ and has absolute Jacobian one. The actual $L^1$ change-of-variables formula [[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]], applied to the restriction $g\\mathbf1_{B_{2R}}$, therefore gives $\\int_{B_R}g(x-y)dy\\le K_R$. Hence\n$$\\int_{B_R}\\int_{B_R}g(x-y)dy\\,dx\\le\\lambda_3(B_R)K_R<\\infty.$$\nThe ball has finite measure by [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]], and the bound uses [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]. The product integrand is Borel: subtraction is continuous, the assigned kernel is Borel and the smooth density factors are Borel. Under [[thm-euclidean-lebesgue-measure-is-the-completion-of-the-product-of-lebesgue-measures]], its Euclidean and product-measure interpretations agree; in particular it is measurable for the product sigma-algebra, so [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] applies before finiteness has been established. Multiplying the displayed bound by $\\|u\\|_\\infty\\|v\\|_\\infty$ proves absolute finiteness of $\\iint\\langle u(x),v(y)\\rangle/(4\\pi|x-y|)$ (with assigned diagonal value), and [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] permits either order. For any fixed $x$, compact bounded $v$ has an everywhere-finite Newtonian integral: choose a ball containing $x-\\operatorname{supp}v$ and bound the translated kernel integral there as above. The same estimate applies to $u$. Thus the pointwise $Nu,Nv$ of [[def-newtonian-potential]] are legitimate, and $|u\\cdot Nv|\\le\\int |u(x)|\\,|v(y)|g(x-y)/(4\\pi)dy$ makes both outer pairings integrable by the already-proved bound ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]] componentwise). Fubini identifies them with the common double integral. Exchanging the variables gives symmetry because $g(x-y)=g(y-x)$ and the Euclidean pairing is symmetric; finite linearity of the two integrals gives bilinearity ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). The arbitrary diagonal assignment changes each section only at one null point and does not change these integrals, as in the Newtonian/kernel interfaces. The choice cost is exactly the declared AComega of the translated Lebesgue, ball, kernel and product-measure interfaces.",

        "statement": "Assume Countable Choice ($\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$) as carried by the Newtonian, polar and Lebesgue interfaces cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\\mu_0>0$ be a real scalar parameter, let $J\\in C_c^\\infty(\\mathbb R^3;\\mathbb R^3)$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $\\operatorname{div}J=0$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), and define componentwise\n$$A:=\\mu_0N(J),\\qquad A_i=\\mu_0\\,N(J_i),\\qquad N f(x)=\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\frac{f(y)}{4\\pi|x-y|}\\,d\\lambda_3(y),$$\nthe Newtonian vector potential of [[def-newtonian-potential]]. Then:\n(a) $A\\in C^2(\\mathbb R^3;\\mathbb R^3)$ with $\\operatorname{div}A=0$ and $-\\Delta A=\\mu_0J$ pointwise on $\\mathbb R^3$, componentwise ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]);\n(b) there is $C>0$ with $|\\operatorname{curl}A(x)|\\le C/(1+|x|^2)$ for every $x\\in\\mathbb R^3$; hence $\\operatorname{curl}A\\in L^2(\\mathbb R^3;\\mathbb R^3)$ and $\\langle A,J\\rangle\\in L^1(\\mathbb R^3)$, both in the ordinary Lebesgue sense ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]);\n(c) the curl-field energy identity\n$$\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}|\\operatorname{curl}A|^2\\,d\\lambda_3=\\mu_0\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\langle A,J\\rangle\\,d\\lambda_3$$\nholds, and equivalently $\\frac12\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\langle A,J\\rangle\\,d\\lambda_3=\\frac1{2\\mu_0}\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}|\\operatorname{curl}A|^2\\,d\\lambda_3\\ge0$.\nThe identity is stated for the explicit smooth compact currents and the Newtonian construction; no uniqueness, no decay of $A$ itself beyond the curl bound of (b), and no extension to singular currents is claimed.",
        "strategy": "**Proof technique:** the differentiated Newtonian identities, decay estimates, and one ball excision with a vanishing boundary flux. 1.1 By [[lem-em-smooth-newtonian-upgrade]] each $A_i=\\mu_0N(J_i)$ is smooth, $-\\Delta A_i=\\mu_0J_i$ and $D^\\alpha A_i=\\mu_0N(D^\\alpha J_i)$ for every multi-index; hence $\\operatorname{div}A=\\sum_i\\partial_iA_i=\\mu_0N(\\operatorname{div}J)=0$ pointwise and $A\\in C^\\infty$, which proves (a) ([[def-newtonian-potential]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). 1.2 Decay: choose $R>0$ with $\\operatorname{supp}J\\subseteq B_R(0)$; the far-field asymptotics of the scalar Newtonian potential ([[thm-decay-of-the-newtonian-potential-of-compactly-supported-data]]) give $|A_i(x)|\\le c_1\\|J_i\\|_1/|x|$ for $|x|>2R$, and the far-field gradient bound ([[lem-em-newtonian-far-field-gradient]] with $n=3$) gives $|\\nabla A_i(x)|\\le c_2\\|J_i\\|_1/|x|^2$ there; since $|\\operatorname{curl}A|^2\\le2\\sum_i|\\nabla A_i|^2\\le6\\max_i|\\nabla A_i|^2$ off the support and $A$ is smooth on the compact region $\\overline B_{2R}(0)$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), the bound of (b) follows with a constant adjusted on the compact part ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). 1.3 The pointwise identity $\\operatorname{div}(A\\times\\operatorname{curl}A)=\\langle\\operatorname{curl}A,\\operatorname{curl}A\\rangle-\\langle A,\\operatorname{curl}\\operatorname{curl}A\\rangle$ holds on $\\mathbb R^3$ ([[lem-the-divergence-and-curl-of-a-cross-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and $\\operatorname{curl}\\operatorname{curl}A=\\nabla\\operatorname{div}A-\\Delta A=\\mu_0J$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]], step 1.1). 1.4 For every $r>2R$ the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]) on the ball $B_r(0)$, whose actual bounded smooth domain and outward normal are supplied by [[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]], gives $\\oint_{\\partial B_r}(A\\times\\operatorname{curl}A)\\cdot\\nu\\,dS=\\int_{B_r}|\\operatorname{curl}A|^2-\\mu_0\\int_{B_r}\\langle A,J\\rangle$, and the boundary flux is bounded by $C_S r^2\\cdot c_3r^{-3}=C_Sc_3/r\\to0$: the finite sphere charts of the ball lemma show that scaling $x=r\\omega$ multiplies each graph surface integral by $r^2$, so its finite area is $C_Sr^2$ with $C_S=\\operatorname{area}(S_1)<\\infty$ by the decay bounds of step 1.2 ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]]). 1.5 Let $r\\to\\infty$. The nonnegative functions $|\\operatorname{curl}A|^2\\mathbf 1_{B_r}$ increase to $|\\operatorname{curl}A|^2$, so their integrals converge to $\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}|\\operatorname{curl}A|^2$ by monotone convergence ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]); $\\langle A,J\\rangle$ is supported in $\\overline B_R$ and continuous, hence integrable, and $\\int_{B_r}\\langle A,J\\rangle\\to\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\\langle A,J\\rangle$ by dominated convergence ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]). Substituting into step 1.4 and letting $r\\to\\infty$ gives (c). Countable Choice is inherited only through the cited Newtonian, polar and Lebesgue supplier interfaces. For the monotone-convergence step use a sequence $r_n\\uparrow\\infty$, $r_n>2R$. The right side of the ball identity tends to the finite compact-source pairing while its boundary flux tends to zero; thus the increasing nonnegative curl-square integrals have a finite limit. Monotone convergence proves $\\operatorname{curl}A\\in L^2$ as well as the identity, without a separately presumed integrable radial majorant. The estimate $|\\operatorname{curl}A|^2\\le2\\sum_i|\\nabla A_i|^2$ follows by applying $(a-b)^2\\le2a^2+2b^2$ to its three coordinate differences. The source-pairing limit has the genuine integrable majorant $|A\\cdot J|$, compactly supported and bounded.",

**A page (8 items, in manifest order).**

- `lem-em-separated-phasor-calculus` (lemma, mathematics; scaffold-added). Real-part calculus of
  separated phasor fields $\operatorname{Re}(\tilde F(x_1,x_2)e^{i(\beta x_3-\omega t)})$:
  the $\partial_{x_j}$, $\partial_{x_3}$, $\partial_t$, divergence and curl identities, and
  the amplitude-injectivity determinant argument with its open-set consequence. This is the
  vehicle that turns the real macroscopic equations into complex amplitude equations without
  ever moving an amplitude's phase by hand.

  identities used throughout G1: $\operatorname{div}(e_z\times\nabla_t h)=0$,
  $\operatorname{curl}(e_z\times\nabla_t h)=e_z\Delta_t h$,
  $e_z\times(e_z\times\nabla_t h)=-\nabla_t h$, the orthogonality and norm identities, and the
  curl/divergence of $z$-independent transverse fields.
- `lem-em-rectangle-mode-profile-identities` (lemma, mathematics; scaffold-added). The
  profiles $h_{mn}=\cos\cos$, $e_{mn}=\sin\sin$: eigen-identities, Neumann/Dirichlet boundary
  traces, orthogonality, exact norms $\frac{L_1L_2}{4}(1+\delta_{m0})(1+\delta_{n0})$ and
  $\frac{L_1L_2}{4}$, and the Dirichlet-type integral identities
  $\int|\nabla h|^2=k_c^2\int h^2$, $\int|\nabla e|^2=k_c^2\int e^2$. Choice-free finite
  computation; consumes the published sine/cosine derivative and addition-formula items.

  cosine and sine systems are complete orthogonal systems of $L^2$ on an interval and on a

  Countable Choice declared and used exactly as in those suppliers.

        "statement": "Assume the lossless isotropic scalar constant branch of [[post-em-material-closure]], the macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] with $\\rho_f=0$, $J_f=0$, and the straight-guide, TEM and separated-phasor conventions of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]]; put $Z:=\\sqrt{\\mu/\\varepsilon}$ and $v:=(\\varepsilon\\mu)^{-1/2}$.\n(a) [Potential form] Let $A\\subseteq\\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded connected $C^1$ domain and let $\\varphi\\in C^2(\\overline A;\\mathbb C)$ (with real-valued potentials included) satisfy $\\Delta\\varphi=0$ on $A$ (the plane Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]; a $C^2$ function with $\\Delta\\varphi=0$ is called harmonic).   affine model are canonically identified with V, the page defines the flat covariant derivative
  by chart-independent component differentiation (no Christoffel symbols), with torsion
  freeness, metric compatibility and zero curvature proved directly from affine chart
  transitions and mixed-partial symmetry. This is what makes the kinematic decomposition,
  Fermi–Walker transport and the Herglotz–Noether coframe computation self-contained in the
  affine model and avoids importing GR connection theorems; the G2 argument of the research
  module (which works in a general Lorentzian manifold) is specialized here to the flat case.

  linear system `X' = M(tau) X` with `M^a_b = c^{-2}(U^a A_b - A^a U_b)`; existence and
  uniqueness on all of I follow from
  `lem-linear-matrix-odes-have-unique-global-solutions-on-a-given-interval` on compact
  subintervals plus uniqueness/patching (equivalently `def-maximal-ode-solution` and

  rescaling is Killing" needs "closed 1-form on a simply connected open set has a primitive".

1. **Giulini Section 5.5 read at statement level; two defects avoided.** The local copy
   `advanced-sources/giulini-rigidity.pdf` (arXiv math-ph/0602018, 614463 bytes, sha16
   `f03fcc87fbfd60fc`, 66 pages) was inspected over Section 5.5 pp. 41–49. The source (a) proves
   the Herglotz–Noether classification only after *assuming analyticity* in the companion proof
   route quoted by Crowell p. 209, and (b) builds a global quotient by the orbits, assuming the
   quotient is a manifold. The S11 research argument used here avoids both: the classification
   is proved smoothly on flow boxes with the slice Levi–Civita connection supplied by
   `thm-fundamental-theorem-of-riemannian-geometry`, Lemma 16's omitted proof is supplied by the
   adapted-coframe computation, and the global rescaling is obtained from the closed 1-form
   primitive rather than the orbit quotient. These scope limits are recorded in the coverage
   rows and in the item statements.
2. **Research-module coefficient discrepancy in S10 (recorded, resolved by direct computation).**
   The S10 research text states `s^a s^b partial_a n_b = gamma^3 q' q''/c^3` for the Bell
   translated congruence. Direct recomputation in the (-+++) convention with `n = gamma(1,q'/c)`
   and the unit longitudinal rest vector `s = gamma(q'/c,1)` gives
   `theta(s,s) = (2 + gamma^2 (q'/c)^2) gamma^3 q' q''/c^3`; the extra positive factor
   `2 + gamma^2 beta^2` does not change the qualitative conclusion (nonzero exactly when
   `q' q'' != 0`), and the scaffold states the recomputed value in
   `thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples` (d) and in the worked Bell example. The
   research module is research context, not a published item; the exact computation is recorded
   here so that Step 3 re-derives it and the owner can decide whether to repair the module.

### Why the four added prerequisites are necessary (recorded, not silent)

- **F5 names an object it must define.** The design's PEC theorem assumes a
  "smooth incident source-free Maxwell phasor near O". The framework had no
  general monochromatic phasor class (only plane-wave and guide-specific
  encodings), so `def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors` fixes the class and
  `lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence` supplies the exact
  Re-calculus/injectivity needed to deduce the smooth-branch real Maxwell
  equations from the phasor system. Both are used only by this pair.

  a prescribed monochromatic electric dipole in vacuum, no independent
  magnetic/higher multipole radiation"; the retarded-fields companion adopted a
  similar idealization inline in an example that cannot be consumed across

  reusable, including its exact leading-term relation to

  status.

  affine classification of the solutions of `z''=Re(w e^{-iωt})`

## Local closure decisions

- The page supplies every prerequisite of its own claims in-page, on top of the in-run
  closure `sr-spacetime-primitives` (batch 1), `sr-lorentz-transformations` (batch 2),
  `sr-worldlines-and-clocks` (batch 3) and `sr-observer-measurements` (batch 4) plus the
  published imported mathematics on disk.
- **The causal signal restriction is a new postulate, and it is the minimal one needed.**
  The design's physical theorem presupposes that "signal" is a model notion; the reader
  report (`reader-taylor/report.md`) states the required distinction explicitly: "The
  operational claim that information propagates only on future causal curves is an adopted
  physical restriction, distinct from merely defining this cone." The postulate is sourced to
  Tolman Section 52 (the order reversal of a superluminal causal impulse and the blocks
  caveat), Carroll Chapter 4 p. 125 ("no signals can travel faster than the speed of light;
  therefore 'information' will only flow along timelike or null trajectories") and Crowell
  Section 4.7.1 (superluminal information transfer and the antitelephone), with the two
  caveats recorded: (i) Crowell's own Section 2.1.3 postulate P1 is a different, existence-style
  statement and is not re-minted; (ii) the source's heuristic argument is not a proof, and the
  item states the restriction as adopted.
- **The flat proper-time maximum is proved, not cited.** Reall Section 2.3 pp. 28–30 states
  the maximization of proper time along straight timelike lines without proof (also noted in
  the reader report). Clause (e) supplies the proof: a passive boost
  `B(beta)`, `beta = v_s/v^0`, maps `D = q - p` to `T e_0`; in that chart the integrand
  satisfies `sqrt(a^2 - b^2) <= a`, integration over the pieces gives `c^{-1} sum tau_i <= T/c`,
  and equality forces the spatial derivative to vanish, i.e. the monotone straight segment.
  The boost construction (`e'_a = B(beta)^{-1} e_a` is an inertial basis because
  `B(beta)^{-1}` is proper orthochronous) is written out in the strategy.
- **Non-claims kept explicit.** (i) The definition item asserts no property of `<=`, `J^+`
  or `R^+`. (ii) The theorem asserts nothing about partial differential equations or
  propagation of particular fields (the research module's "no PDE finite propagation" scope
  clause). (iii) The spacelike lemma says nothing about synchronization procedures; "the two
  events are simultaneous in the frame" is equality of the frame's time coordinate. (iv) The
  postulate and the thought experiment carry their availability assumptions and the
  non-signal patterns (Tolman's blocks, moving spots, prearranged triggers) explicitly outside
  their conclusions. (v) The two B counterexamples refute specific displayed statements
  (frame independence of spacelike time order; "causally related implies timelike-joinable"),
  not "classical physics" or any framework.
- **Axiom of choice.** No batch-5 item uses AC or a countable-choice principle: the arguments
  are finite-dimensional coordinate algebra, one explicit boost, integrals of continuous
  functions on compact intervals and finite sums. No choice declaration is needed or made.
- **Units.** Mathematical items treat `c` as a fixed positive constant of the model and use

## Source findings (exact evidence)

1. **Crowell Section 4.7.1 (arXiv-equivalent pp. 110–111) is an argument sketch.** Arguments
   1–4 are presented as a "defense in depth"; argument 1 is explicitly called the weakest
   ("we have no strong reasons for believing in causality as an overarching principle"). The
   page therefore adopts the restriction as a postulate and records the heuristic status in
   the postulate's clause (iii) and in the coverage row.
2. **Crowell's P1 (Section 2.1.3 p. 44) is not this page's postulate.** P1 asserts the
   existence of events whose displacement is timelike in all frames; the causal signal
   restriction asserts that no signal connects spacelike-related events. The difference is
   recorded in the coverage row and here; no ID is reused.
3. **Tolman Section 52 (pp. 54–55) is a one-way computation in an older notation.** Formula
   (29) gives the negative elapsed time for a superluminal causal impulse in a moving system;
   the two-way closed chain is supplied locally by
   `texp-sr-superluminal-relay-antitelephone` and its worked arithmetic (B page), and
   Tolman's caveat that kinematic occurrences without causal connection are not restricted is
   realized as `ex-sr-superluminal-sweep-has-no-causal-connection`.
4. **Reall Section 2.3 pp. 28–30 states maximality without proof** ("It can be shown that
   these lines maximize the proper time between two points"); the page proves it (see above)
   and the coverage row records the source's status.
5. **Carroll Chapter 4 pp. 124–127 material on domains of dependence and Misner space is not
   used as a supplier.** The domain-of-dependence discussion concerns PDE initial-value
   problems (deferred to `em-vacuum-waves-and-polarization`), and Misner space is not the
   affine model (out-of-scope). The reader report's warning about "signals inside the light
   cone" being an adopted principle is what the postulate records.

  disk (Riemann/Darboux integrals and the FTC suppliers, finite sums, finite Cauchy–Schwarz, the
  vector-valued derivative/integral and norm-inequality items, square-root and monotonicity items,
  the induction principle, coordinates with respect to a basis).
- **The corner hypothesis (H), and why it is stated.** Batch 3's piecewise C^1 definition
  ("C^1 on the open pieces and one-sided derivatives at the partition points exist") does not by
  itself make the piecewise proper-time integral well defined: a derivative that is continuous on an
  open interval can be unbounded at the endpoints and fail to be Riemann integrable (the same
  phenomenon the library records in `cex-a-function-with-a-primitive-that-is-not-integrable`, and
  the reason `thm-ftc-second-part` carries an integrability hypothesis). SR06 therefore states its
  own corner hypothesis (H): each piece's derivative has finite one-sided limits at both endpoints,
  i.e. extends continuously to the closed piece. This is the library's standard piecewise-C^1
  convention (`def-piecewise-c-one-curve-on-a-manifold`), it is automatic for every piecewise
  inertial worldline (the extended derivative is the constant d_i), and it makes the piecewise
  integral, the per-piece Newton–Leibniz increment and the endpoint bound well defined by
  additivity. The non-(H) piecewise case is deliberately outside the pair's scope. This is recorded
  as an interface observation for the owner; it requires no change to any batch-3 item, since no
  batch-3 claim is restated or weakened here.
- **Interface observation on the batch-3 clock postulate.** `post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-
  hypothesis` (ii) states the clock hypothesis for piecewise C^1 histories "with finitely many
  kinks" and attaches the reading to the proper-time difference of `def-sr-proper-time`, which is
  stated there for C^1 worldlines. SR06 supplies the missing piecewise object for the class (H) in
  `def-sr-piecewise-proper-time` and both physics items read the clock hypothesis through it. No
  wording of the batch-3 item is changed (it is out of this batch's scope); the observation is
  recorded for owner reconciliation.

**Convention check across the three sources (recorded because the transverse protocol is
the trap S5 warns about).** All three formulas agree once the velocity sign and angle
convention are fixed. Einstein's `phi` is the angle between the source–observer line (the
propagation direction `s`) and the observer's velocity, so `cos(phi) = beta_hat . s` and his
formula is the theorem's `omega' = gamma(1 - beta.s) omega`; his `phi = pi/2` gives
`cos(phi') = -|beta|`, the theorem's clause (v). Crowell's §6.5.1 `theta` is the angle
between the propagation direction and the source's velocity relative to the observer
(equivalently the negative of the observer's velocity), as fixed by his own 1+1 example
(wave left, observer right, shift D > 1); his formula `omega' = gamma omega (1 + v cos
theta)` is then exactly `gamma(1 - beta.s) omega`. Murugesh's `omega'_k' =
gamma_0 omega_k (1 - k_hat . beta_0)` has the same reading. The **transverse** statements,
however, split by protocol exactly as the theorem's clause (iv) states: Einstein's
`phi = pi/2` and Crowell's §6.5.1 `theta = 90` give `omega' = gamma omega` (wave transverse
to the relative velocity in the source frame), while Crowell's §3.2 "purely transverse…
1/gamma" remark and Murugesh's §6.1.2 (`k' . v_0 = 0` in the observer's frame) give
`omega' = omega/gamma` (transverse in the receiver frame). The pair therefore states both
protocols with the equivalence `beta.s = |beta|^2 <=> s'.beta_hat = 0`; the B-page example
and counterexample compute both factors at `beta = 3/5`. No source defect is claimed for
this: the readings are consistent once the protocol is stated, and the coverage rows record
the exact conversion.
**Errata/limits recorded, not harvested as claims:** Crowell Example 1 (Ives–Stilwell
frequencies and uncertainties), Example 2 (Bertozzi time-of-flight data) and Example 6
(Heckmann plates, 0.00 ± 0.06″) are reported measurements; they are deferred to
`sr-experimental-interface` for primary-report, calibration and statistical work. Crowell
Example 7 (optical appearance of a moving cube) and §6.6.2 (group velocity) are
out-of-scope for a single monochromatic plane-wave model. Einstein's amplitude/intensity
transformation is out-of-scope for the same reason. No experiment, measurement or
statistical statement is authored on this pair.

        "statement": "Let $(A,V,\\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$; let $E_n,q_n$ be as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].\n(a) For every $P\\in\\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ the coordinate components of $P$ in the frame are $(P^0,P^1,P^2,P^3)=(E_n(P)/c,\\,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, where $q_n(P)=\\sum_{i=1}^3q^ie_i$; if $P$ is future timelike then $E^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\\sum_{i=1}^3(q^i)^2$ with $E=E_n(P)$.\n(b) Let $x:I\\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline whose chart coordinate path is $t\\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w:=r'$ and $\\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; then $|w|<c$, the four-velocity is $U=\\gamma_w(c,w)$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\\,(e), and for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant the components are $P=m\\gamma_w(c,w)$, that is $E_n(P)=m\\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=\\sum_{i=1}^3m\\gamma_ww^ie_i$.\n(c) Let $B(\\beta)$ be the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $\\beta=v/c$, $|v|<c$, along a spatial direction $s$, and let $P'$ denote the components of the same vector $P$ after the coordinate change $x'=B(\\beta)x$; write $\\mathbf p=(P^1,P^2,P^3)$ and split it into its components $\\mathbf p_\\parallel$, $\\mathbf p_\\perp$ with respect to $s$.         "statement": "Let $(A,V,\\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $x:I\\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline with proper-time function $\\tau:I\\to J$ and inverse $\\rho:J\\to I$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).\n(a) For a $C^1$ map $P:I\\to V$ define its proper-time derivative $\\dot P:I\\to V$ by\n$$\\dot P(s):=\\frac{P'(s)}{\\tau'(s)},$$\nwhere $P'$ is the derivative of $P$ with respect to the worldline parameter, taken componentwise in any affine basis of $V$; the result does not depend on the basis because two affine bases differ by a constant invertible linear map. Equivalently $\\dot P(s)=(P\\circ\\rho)'(\\tau(s))$, so $\\dot P$ is the derivative of the proper-time parametrised field $P\\circ\\rho$. Since $\\tau'(s)>0$ by [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]], $\\dot P$ is well defined and continuous whenever $P$ is $C^1$.\n(b) If $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ the four-velocity of $x$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), then $F:=\\dot P$ is called the four-force on the particle; in an inertial frame $F$ has the components of the derivative of the four-momentum with respect to proper time.\n(c) This item introduces a derivative and a name only. (b) If $f:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ is $C^1$ and compactly supported and $g:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ is $C^1$, then for each $a$, $\\int_\\Omega(\\partial_af)g\\,d^4x=-\\int_\\Omega f(\\partial_ag)\\,d^4x$, provided $g$ is $C^1$ on $\\Omega$ and the products are extended by zero outside $\\operatorname{supp}f$. (c) If $F:(-s_0,s_0)\\times\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ is continuous with continuous $\\partial_sF$ and there is a compact $K\\Subset\\Omega$ with $F(s,z)=0$ for $z\\notin K$ and all $s$, then $s\\mapsto\\int_\\Omega F(s,z)\\,d^4z$ is $C^1$ on $(-s_0,s_0)$ with derivative $\\int_\\Omega\\partial_sF(s,z)\\,d^4z$.
